primary_crosschecks.verified: ACL 2026 PIArena is peer reviewed and releases code. The paper explicitly introduces a defense-feedback-guided adaptive strategy attack and reports substantially higher ASR than Direct/Combined across the evaluated defense suite; exact worker-reported aggregate values are consistent with the paper tables. This is a threat-model comparison, not an isolated estimate of adaptivity alone.

PIArena Table 5 ports the same defense modules across InjecAgent, AgentDojo, AgentDyn and WASP and shows large ASR/utility variation. Because benchmark tasks, backends and attack protocols differ, this is direct portability evidence but not a single-factor benchmark-identity causal effect.

PIArena reports near-zero adaptive-strategy ASR for AttentionTracker while average no-attack utility is about 15%; the paper itself highlights the utility cost. This directly demonstrates that ASR-only ranking can favor denial/refusal behavior under this benchmark contract.

arXiv:2604.23887 reports an adaptive attacker evolving over hundreds of rounds, more than 20,000 attacks, eventual failure of every model-reliant defense, and zero exact-secret leaks for deterministic output filtering across 15,000 attacks. Exact round-to-break values remain author-primary and were not independently rerun here.

arXiv:2604.12198 reports 111 open-access computational-physics papers, 88 substantive critiques, and 86/88 = 97.7% surfacing only after execution; it also reports a 12-paper two-machine cross-check with overlapping critique categories on 7/12. This supports execution-grounded defect discovery but is not a matched mandatory-gate ablation.

microsoft/regorus PR #718 was merged on 2026-05-18 and explicitly documents two independent faults for dynamic-key partial-object rules: interpreter early-return dropped bindings and RVM rule classification misidentified the rule type. The PR adds interpreter/RVM regressions and fallbacks for unsupported patterns.

The PLOS Computational Biology article was published 2026-08-25 and provides the SPLiT constrained/unconstrained recurrent model plus supporting code archive. The sealed worker's algebraic check is exact at the stated equation level: for orthonormal Q and orthogonal kxk R, span(QR)=span(Q) and (QR)(QR)^T=QQ^T; elementwise tanh does not generically preserve an arbitrary dense linear subspace. This narrows interpretation pending code-level inspection rather than refuting the paper.

Wang-Ramdas provide anytime-valid Gaussian-mean constructions with unknown variance; Safe Testing establishes e-value safety under optional continuation; conditional CTM work provides a fixed-reference anytime-valid shift detector. None of those sources directly proves the worker's frozen-reference repeated-block/common-increment delayed-start construction. The worker's late-change dominance is therefore engineering evidence within its simulated Gaussian grid, not inherited theorem-level generality.

assessments.tested_scope: PIArena's released datasets, defense suite, Qwen3-4B-Instruct attacker/default settings, and Direct/Combined/Strategy threat-model comparison.
assessments.rationale: Peer-reviewed primary evidence with an official implementation shows that a defense-feedback-guided adaptive search can sharply increase ASR relative to the released static/heuristic baselines, including very large changes for PISanitizer and other defenses. This strongly supports evaluating defenses under defense-specific adaptive pressure. The Strategy arm also changes search procedure and query use, so the result is not a single-factor causal estimate of adaptivity alone.
limits: No independent numerical rerun of the full table in this comparator invocation.
Adaptive and static arms do not hold search budget/procedure fixed as one isolated factor.
Generalization beyond the released PIArena task/defense/model settings is unproven.

assessments.tested_scope: PIArena Table-5 ports of the listed defense modules to InjecAgent, AgentDojo, AgentDyn and the paper's static 84-case WASP extraction.
assessments.rationale: The same named defense modules show materially different ASR and utility across four agentic benchmark integrations, so treating one benchmark headline as a portable defense property is empirically unsafe. However, backend models, tasks, attack protocols and WASP execution semantics differ across columns; this is a real portability failure observation, not a matched causal estimate of benchmark identity alone.
limits: Multiple factors change across benchmark ports.
WASP is evaluated as a reduced static single-page protocol rather than its full live environment.
No independent rerun in this comparator invocation.

assessments.tested_scope: PIArena aggregate defense evaluation and its no-attack utility metric under the released task mix, especially AttentionTracker under the Strategy attack.
assessments.rationale: This is a direct matched metric-design counterexample: the defense with near-zero adaptive-strategy ASR can retain only about 15% average no-attack utility. An ASR-only objective would therefore reward a system that often withholds or breaks normal task completion. The evidence strongly supports joint safety-plus-utility scoring under this benchmark contract.
limits: The exact utility definition is PIArena-specific and detection defenses may intentionally abstain.
This does not show that AttentionTracker is globally inferior or that abstention is never desirable.
No external replication of the exact aggregate table was performed here.

assessments.tested_scope: arXiv:2604.23887's direct system-prompt secret-extraction threat model, nine defense configurations, evolutionary attacker and reported extended campaigns.
assessments.rationale: More than 20,000 attacks over hundreds of adaptive rounds provide substantial author-primary evidence that short campaigns can miss delayed catastrophic failures of model-reliant prompt defenses. The two-phase quiet-then-break pattern is decision-relevant for horizon design. But exact time-to-break is not reported as a multi-seed survival distribution and the endpoint is deterministic exact-secret leakage, so broad security durability claims would exceed scope.
limits: Preprint rather than peer-reviewed publication at the frozen snapshot.
Round-to-break measurements are not a multi-seed distribution for each defense.
Threat model and scoring focus on known embedded secrets, not arbitrary indirect/semantic exfiltration.

assessments.tested_scope: The 111-paper computational-physics corpus and the paper's post-hoc phase classification of 88 substantive critiques in the read-plan-compute-compare loop.
assessments.rationale: The scale and phase attribution are strong for the narrow observation that nearly all substantive critiques in this corpus surfaced only after calculations were executed and compared. The two-machine subset adds some convergence evidence. But the proposed reproduce-before-promote gate is an adaptation: there is no matched same-model/tools/budget comparison showing that making re-execution mandatory improves terminal scientific decisions.
limits: Phase labels were assigned post hoc rather than randomized by review mode.
Computational physics with executable numerical ground truth may not transfer to non-executable science.
The candidate's mandatory gate itself lacks a matched causal ablation.

assessments.tested_scope: microsoft/regorus PR #718 dynamic-key partial-object-rule behavior and the interpreter/RVM defects fixed by the merged patch.
assessments.rationale: A merged primary-source bug report with an exact reproducer identifies two distinct implementation errors affecting the same realistic Rego construct, one in the ordinary interpreter and one in RVM classification. Regression tests and fallback guards make the defect concrete and reproducible from project history. This strongly raises the value of generated interpreter-vs-RVM differential testing, but one historical bug does not quantify current mismatch frequency or prove a proposed fuzzer's benefit.
limits: Historical fixed bug rather than evidence of current-main failure on the repaired cases.
Single defect family cannot estimate the overall semantic-drift rate.
Generated replayable fuzzing remains a proposed next experiment, not an evaluated mechanism.

assessments.tested_scope: Godin-Thivierge SPLiT paper as published 2026-08-25, plus the sealed worker's exact linear-algebra checks on the printed structural-manifold rotation/confinement equations; not a code-level reproduction of S8/S11/S12.
assessments.rationale: The paper provides peer-reviewed simulations, analytical results and a supporting code archive for manifold-constrained plasticity. Separately, the equation-level audit establishes two precise scope constraints: right multiplication Q->QR cannot rotate span(Q) in ambient space, and rank-k recurrent W alone does not force elementwise tanh dynamics to remain in an arbitrary dense span(Q). These are mathematically strong reasons to defer interpretation of the rotational-drift/confinement experiments until exact code semantics are inspected, not a refutation of SPLiT's reported performance.
limits: Official code archive bytes were not inspected in the sealed worker run because download transport was blocked.
The algebraic tension may be resolved by projections or different implemented dynamics.
No independent numerical reproduction of the published effect sizes was performed.

assessments.tested_scope: The sealed worker's iid Gaussian KL=1 finite direction grid, frozen-reference block construction, delayed-start common-increment recursion and reported common-random Monte Carlo at immediate/1k/10k/100k changepoints.
assessments.rationale: The candidate has useful same-simulator common-random evidence that the delayed-start architecture avoids late-change wealth decay and can dominate the earlier fixed-reference CTM route at long prechange horizons. Established e-value/CTM literature supports the general anytime-valid ingredients. The candidate-specific repeated reuse filtration, four-direction factor construction, continuum KL>=1 guarantee and numerical constants are worker-derived; the stronger nuisance-aware mean factor is explicitly unproved. Evidence therefore remains engineering-level rather than externally theorem-complete.
limits: Finite Gaussian KL=1 grid, not the full KL>=1 continuum or non-Gaussian/dependent shifts.
Monte Carlo and arbitrary-precision checks are not independent replication or machine-directed interval proofs.
Published safe-t/CTM guarantees cannot be transplanted to the exact frozen-reference reuse filtration without a fresh conditional-e proof.
